transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Meeting type: Partner co-sell / pipeline & deal strategy workshop
Shared artifacts: Deck: http://bit.ly/mosaic-rwd-cosell , Pipeline sheet: https://drive.google.com/mosaic-pipeline (note: access request required)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jon Patel (Redwood SE), Ruth Li (Redwood Channel), Leah Torres (Mosaic Head Partnerships), Diego Morales (Mosaic Channel Sales), Priya Singh (Mosaic SE)

Summary:
Quick sync to prioritize joint accounts, align on pilot + PoV gating criteria, and agree on co-sell motions (referral vs. joint sales). Focus on deal acceleration tactics for four strategic accounts Mosaic is opening in EMEA. Discussed technical validation (sandbox perf), pricing anchor, and channel margin expectations. Action items assigned for collateral, sandbox runs, and intro to SDRs.

Topics:
- Account prioritization and swimlanes
- Joint pilot / PoV success criteria
- Technical validation plan (latency/cost targets)
- Commercial motion: referral vs co-sell vs reseller
- Compliance/infosec checklist for enterprise customers

Transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood): All right, everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, we're on the 15:00 UTC slot, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intros? We'll go round-robin, then jump into the pipeline sheet.
00:08 Leah (Mosaic): Hi, Leah here, head of partnerships at Mosaic. Diego and Priya on the call as well. Thanks Maya.
00:12 Diego (Mosaic): Diego — channel sales, hi all.
00:15 Priya (Mosaic): Priya, solutions eng.
00:17 Jon (Redwood): Jon, SE at Redwood. I'll drive the technical part and the sandbox run details.
00:20 Ruth (Redwood): Ruth, channel, I'll own the co-sell ops and handoffs.
00:23 Maya (Redwood): Great. Main goals for today: two things — pick top accounts for a Q2 acceleration push and agree on what a successful PoV looks like. Also resolve the question of whether we do pure referral or joint close for each account.
00:35 Leah (Mosaic): Cool, high level — Mosaic's seeing interest from four enterprise logos in EMEA, two in financial services and two in retail. We think Redwood's latency and cost story is compelling but the procurement teams want SAML/SSO, audit logs, and clarity on data residency.
00:50 Maya (Redwood): Good callout. We have SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO, KMS integrations. For data residency we can host in eu-west region or do Private deployment if needed — that usually comes up on the banking customers.
01:04 Diego (Mosaic): Question — how fast can a Private deployment be stood up? Our banks want a 6-week window for gating approval.
01:11 Jon (Redwood): 6 weeks is tight but doable for a scoped Private engagement — depends on infra pre-reqs (VPC peering, HSM/KMS setup). For a faster start we recommend a hosted PoV with strict contract and data retention rules, then move to Private for production. There's a small chance I said KV cash earlier in internal notes, but I mean KV cache.
01:32 Priya (Mosaic): Yeah we had a line in our internal doc about "KV cash or cache" and it sounded off — thanks for clarifying. For procurement, they also want support for per-tenant encryption keys.
01:40 Maya (Redwood): We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private; hosted can do tenant-level keying with some restrictions — we'll put exact language in the security appendix we share.
01:50 Leah (Mosaic): Great. On the commercial motion — for two of these accounts the Mosaic exec sponsor wants joint sell (we get co-credit), for the other two they'd prefer we act as referral and Mosaic handle the close.
02:03 Ruth (Redwood): Let's map that to deal complexity. For strategic deals where Redwood needs to run performance tests or a PoV, joint close makes sense. For smaller deals referral might be better. We should codify thresholds — ARR > $250k and need for Private deployment => joint co-sell.
02:20 Diego (Mosaic): That threshold sounds reasonable but some of our EMEA retail logos are high go-to-market value even if initial ARR is modest. Can we have an exception path?
02:30 Maya (Redwood): Yes — we can add an exceptions committee: Mosaic rep + Ruth + Maya to approve on a case-by-case. Also need to be clear about discounting and margins.
02:40 Leah (Mosaic): Speaking of pricing — what are typical entry price bands for dedicated vs hosted?
02:46 Maya (Redwood): Hosted API is usage-based with per-token pricing. For Dedicated we work with reservation/fixed monthly commit; typical entry reserved commit is around $15k/month for small pools, but for production-banks we usually recommend bigger commits to hit SLA. We'll provide ranges in the one-pager.
03:05 Diego (Mosaic): Ok, please include expected reseller margin or referral percentage in that one-pager.
03:12 Ruth (Redwood): We'll include a partner-friendly revenue share matrix — referral % vs joint % vs reseller margin, we'll also list lead distribution logic.
03:22 Jon (Redwood): On the tech side, here's the plan for validation: Jon to run a 1-hour sandbox perf run simulating typical tokens for each account — we need target latency P95 < 250ms for chat and cost per 1k tokens estimate.
03:37 Priya (Mosaic): For the bank customers, they weigh latency very heavily. They also want deterministic output for certain prompts — is there support for model pinning/rollbacks?
03:46 Jon (Redwood): Yes, model pinning and rollbacks are supported in the platform — you can pin model versions and we do rollout policies. Also we have tracing hooks for inference that help debug regressions.
03:56 Leah (Mosaic): Good. Can we get a short demo for the bank tech committee? Maybe a 30-minute session that includes SSO flow and audit logging?
04:06 Maya (Redwood): Absolutely — we'll schedule an SSO+audit demo. Jon, can you lead that with Priya?
04:10 Jon (Redwood): Yep, happy to.
04:12 Priya (Mosaic): Perfect.
04:15 (Timestamp gap — sharing pipeline doc)
04:18 Maya (Redwood): I'm pulling up the joint pipeline sheet — I put the four target accounts in the top rows. Leah, can you confirm the deal stage and expected close window?
04:26 Leah (Mosaic): Bank A is in "technical review" with expected close Q2 end; Bank B is in procurement with tight timelines Q3; Retail Co X is in early discussions.
04:34 Diego (Mosaic): Retail Co X has a pilot budget but it's under $60k — might be referral.
04:40 Ruth (Redwood): Noted. For Bank A — because they're already in tech review let's prioritize the sandbox perf and security appendix.
04:48 Jon (Redwood): For sandbox we'll need sample prompts, typical sequence lengths, and expected concurrency patterns — Priya can you attach those to the pipeline sheet?
04:56 Priya (Mosaic): Yes I'll add three sample prompts and a concurrency profile by EOD tomorrow.
05:00 Maya (Redwood): Awesome. On PoV success criteria — propose: 1) latency P95 targets met, 2) cost per 1k tokens within agreed band, 3) security checklist accepted by procurement, 4) stakeholder sign-off from product owner. Anything missing?
05:18 Leah (Mosaic): Add behavioral quality checks — we need no more than X% of hallucinations on key prompts, and acceptance tests that validate outputs against a golden set.
05:27 Jon (Redwood): We can run evals against a test set and show regression comparisons; Redwood Optimize can produce baseline reports.
05:33 Diego (Mosaic): Does Redwood do structured output support? The bank wants consistent JSON outputs for downstream processing.
05:38 Jon (Redwood): Yes, we have structured output support and function/tool calling. We'll include examples in the demo.
05:45 (Background noise, brief crosstalk)
06:00 Maya (Redwood): Ok moving to risk and objections — what's Mosaic hearing from customers around vendor preference and procurement blockers?
06:07 Leah (Mosaic): Main blockers: data residency, audit trail, and legal's concern about model weights and IP. Some of them ask why not use Anthropic or Cohere.
06:15 Maya (Redwood): For IP and weights — we emphasize serving-not-training: Redwood doesn't retain training data, and we can provide contractual protections. We'll send a short legal FAQ.
06:27 Ruth (Redwood): Also highlight our fallback and reliability story — graceful degradation to smaller models and routing policies when peak capacity hits. That helps uptime concerns compared to single vendor risks.
06:40 Diego (Mosaic): Great. I want to flag commercial timing — if we push joint co-sell on Bank A we need a draft SOW quickly. Who drafts?
06:48 Maya (Redwood): We'll draft a templated SOW and attach the security appendix. Maya will own initial SOW draft; Ruth will review partner clauses.
06:55 Leah (Mosaic): Can Mosaic legal review and redline within one week? They have a procurement freeze window end of March.
07:02 Maya (Redwood): We'll expedite.
07:05 (crosstalk)
07:20 Jon (Redwood): Quick technical caveat: for Private deployments we may ask for network windows to provision GPUs — lead time can vary if your infra team needs to approve VPC peering.
07:31 Priya (Mosaic): Noted. I'll engage Mosaic infra and include a point person in the sheet.
07:35 Maya (Redwood): Cool. Let's talk about marketing / co-branded GTM — Ruth, you had ideas?
07:41 Ruth (Redwood): Yes — propose a joint case study template and a shared webinar for the first successful pilot. Also recommend a co-sell playbook page that outlines lead routing, ownership, and win credits. We'll co-draft with Mosaic marketing.
07:55 Leah (Mosaic): Webinar sounds high value. Will add to our Q2 demand gen plan.
08:01 Diego (Mosaic): Back to pricing — if Redwood can commit to a pilot discount for the first 90 days, Mosaic can bundle it into its commercial pitch.
08:10 Maya (Redwood): We can offer a one-time pilot credit or discounted commit; exact terms in the one-pager.
08:15 Leah (Mosaic): Good.
08:18 Jon (Redwood): Ok technical next steps: Jon will run the sandbox perf and provide a simple runbook and sample cURLs. Expected deliverable: perf report + sample outputs.
08:27 Maya (Redwood): Commercial next steps: Maya will share the co-sell one-pager, SOW template, and partner revenue-share matrix.
08:33 Priya (Mosaic): I'll share sample prompts and expected concurrency.
08:37 Diego (Mosaic): I'll lock down the top 4 accounts and confirm which are joint vs referral.
08:44 Maya (Redwood): Anything else?
08:47 Leah (Mosaic): Two quick questions: 1) Are there any exclusivity asks? 2) How do we handle multi-region compliance requirements?
08:55 Maya (Redwood): 1) We don't do exclusivity as standard; can discuss bespoke deals. 2) Multi-region is supported via dedicated regions and Private; we'll list specifics in the security appendix.
09:06 (small pause)
09:12 Ruth (Redwood): I'll also introduce Mosaic to two SDRs for joint outreach — Ruth to send intros.
09:18 Maya (Redwood): Great. Any other blockers?
09:22 Priya (Mosaic): None from SE — just need access to the sandbox and runbook.
09:26 Jon (Redwood): We'll provision a sandbox workspace and send creds to Priya by 2026-03-02.
09:33 Maya (Redwood): Sweet. Closing — recap of next steps and owners.
09:38 Maya (Redwood): Recap: Maya share co-sell one-pager and SOW; Jon run perf and share runbook; Priya add prompts and concurrency to pipeline; Diego confirm account split; Ruth intro SDRs and review revenue share.
09:50 Leah (Mosaic): Sounds good, thanks everyone.
09:52 Diego (Mosaic): Thanks all.
09:54 Maya (Redwood): Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the SSO demo and perf run.
09:58 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms (KV cache seen as "KV cash" in earlier notes), speaker overlap a couple times, some timestamps approximate.
